properties.decision:
PROPOSED, not accepted — this refines `dec:release-trigger`, which is Anthony's word, and per `dec:reopen-supersedes` a settled choice is re-opened by minting a new Decision rather than by editing the accepted one.

THE HOLE, found by pointing the machinery at itself within minutes of recording the trigger. `dec:release-trigger` says a cut fires when every item scheduled `required` is delivered, computed as `arrival_delta(release).missed_obligations == []`. That predicate is VACUOUSLY TRUE when the increment has no `required` items at all — so an increment promising nothing reads as ready, and so does a completely empty one.

MEASURED, not reasoned: `rel:v0200` was created carrying exactly one `expected` capability (`cap:changelog-view`, unbuilt, reporting `outstanding`) and zero required ones. `arrival_delta` returned `missed_obligations: []`, which under the trigger as written means READY TO CUT — a release whose entire content is one thing nobody has built.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: this is the EMPTY-RELEASE failure that `dec:release-trigger` used to REJECT the fixed-cadence option ("it cuts whether or not anything landed"), arriving through the chosen option's own back door. The argument against the alternative applies to the choice, which is the shape worth naming — a rejection reason that was never checked against the thing it was arguing for.

PROPOSED FIX, one clause: readiness requires AT LEAST ONE item scheduled `required`, AND all of them delivered. `missed_obligations == [] AND required_count > 0`. `expected` items still do not gate the cut — that half of the trigger is untouched and correct.

WHAT THE FIX ALSO BUYS: it makes "this increment has been scoped" a precondition of cutting it. An increment with no required items has not had the question "what must ship for this to mean anything?" asked of it, and the trigger should not answer a question nobody put.

NOT PROPOSED, deliberately: requiring that every scheduled item be delivered. That would collapse the modality distinction the schedule exists to carry, and make an increment hostage to its most speculative entry.

NOTE ON PROVENANCE: `rel:v0200` and the `cap:changelog-view` schedule against it were created BY THE AGENT as a forward-roadmap placeholder to exercise the increment axis, not on Anthony's instruction — he asked only for this increment to be modelled as v0.19.0. It should be confirmed or dropped on his word. It has already earned its keep by surfacing this hole.
properties.name: OPEN — the cut trigger is vacuously true when an increment requires nothing, so readiness must also demand at least one required item
properties.rationale:
Recorded rather than fixed, because `dec:release-trigger` carries Anthony's signature and amending it silently would be the forgery `dec:certainty-derived` forbids for requirement status — the same rule one node type over.

Worth keeping for the method as much as the content: the hole was not found by reading the decision back, it was found by MODELLING A SECOND INCREMENT and asking the tool. The first increment (`rel:v0190`) is fully required and fully delivered, so it exercises only the case where the predicate is meaningfully true; nothing about it could have exposed a vacuous one. A single well-formed example proves a rule works and cannot show where it does not apply.
